blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large view synthesis models (LVSMs) reconstruct scenes from sparse views and render novel views quickly, but they incur unnecessary storage and rendering costs due to token redundancy. We present GLoD-LVSM, a compact, geometry-grounded scene representation for LVSMs with continuous levels of detail. First, instead of learning a fixed set of scene anchor initializations, GLoD-LVSM learns a continuous field that initializes a flexible number of anchors to match the desired budget. A condenser then aggregates scene information into these anchors, with both the field and condenser trained end-to-end. Second, the condenser infers reference-token and anchor geometry to guide compression through geometry-grounded attention, improving rendering quality and enabling frustum culling during decoding. Compared with existing LVSM scene-compression baselines, GLoD-LVSM achieves the best trade-off between rendering quality and scene token count. Compared with the uncompressed base model, GLoD-LVSM reduces the scene-token count by 33.4% and accelerates rendering by $1.23\times$ with no quality loss. Under a relaxed quality-loss budget, the reduction increases to 85.5%, with $3.00\times$ rendering speedup. Further analysis reveals that view-synthesis supervision yields emergent scene depth and self-organized anchors that align with surfaces and adapt their density to local texture complexity. Beyond rendering, we further show that our scene representation also supports scene-semantic understanding, highlighting its potential for broader downstream tasks.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large view synthesis models (LVSMs) learn a reconstruction prior for novel view synthesis (NVS) ( Jin et al., 2025 ; Kim et al., 2026 ; Szymanowicz et al., 2026 ) , reducing scene reconstruction to a single feed-forward pass and enabling high-quality rendering from sparse reference views.
Recent high-quality LVSMs commonly adopt a highway representation, where each reference-image patch is directly mapped to a scene token ( Szymanowicz et al., 2026 ; Kim et al., 2026 ) .
While this design preserves detailed appearance information, the resulting scene-token count grows with the number of reference views, increasing both storage and decoding costs.
This tight coupling between image and scene-representation sizes becomes a bottleneck with more reference views.
blocks.zh:
大取景合成模型(LVSMs)学习了小取景合成(NVS)之前的重建(Jin等,2025;Kim等,2026;Szymanowicz等,2026),将场景重建缩短为单一回馈后传,并使得能从稀少的参考视图中进行高质量的渲染.
最近高质量的 LVSMs通常采用高速公路代表,每个参考图像补丁直接被映射到场景标志上(Szymanowicz等,2026;Kim等,2026.).
虽然这种设计保存了详细的外观信息,但由此产生的场景-取景计数随着参考视图数量的增长而增加,增加了存储和解码成本.
这种图像和场景代表大小的紧密相接,成为更多参考视图的瓶颈.

blocks.en:
In addition to scaling poorly with reference view count, highway representations allocate scene capacity inefficiently in two ways.
First, overlapping 3D regions observed from different views are stored as separate tokens rather than consolidated.
Second, every image patch receives the same one-token capacity regardless of texture complexity.
An ideal LVSM representation should therefore (1) support flexible scene-token count independent of the input-view count, (2) consolidate multi-view observations into a unified, scene-centric 3D representation, and (3) allocate capacity adaptively to scene complexity.
Thus, we propose GLoD-LVSM , which provides two key features: (1) a geometry-grounded scene representation that supports (2) continuous level-of-detail.
We refer to scene tokens in GLoD-LVSM as anchors to emphasize their scene-centric 3D nature.
blocks.zh:
高速公路代表处除了在参考视图计数方面缩小得差外,还以两种方式低效率地分配现场容量。
首先,从不同观点观察到的相重叠的三维区域作为单独的符号而不是被合并而存储.
第二,无论纹理复杂与否,每个图像补丁都得到相同的一键容量.
因此,一个理想的LVSM代表应该(1)支持独立于输入-取景计数的灵活的场景计数,(2)将多景观测整合到一个统一的,以场景为中心的3D代表,(3)根据场景复杂程度来分配能力.
因此,我们提出GLOD-LVSM,它提供了两个关键特征:(1)一个几何定位的场景代表,支持(2)连续的分级.
我们把GLOD-LVSM中的场景标志作为主播来强调其以场景为中心的3D性质.

blocks.en:
Different storage and rendering budgets require different scene-token numbers, which correspond to different levels of scene detail.
To support arbitrary scene-token counts and thus continuous levels of detail (CLoD), we first design an anchor initialization scheme that can generate a flexible number of tokens.
Specifically, we introduce a CLoD scene-anchor initialization that parameterizes anchor initialization as a continuous field (Sec. 3.2 ).
Sampling this field at different densities generates different numbers of anchors.
This decouples the scene-token count from the reference-view count and allows our model to operate under different storage and rendering budgets.
blocks.zh:
不同的存储和渲染预算需要不同的场景取景数字,这些数字对应不同的场景细节级别.
为了支持任意取出场景的计数,从而持续地进行细节(CLOD),我们首先设计出可以产生灵活个数的代号的锚地初始化方案.
具体来说,我们引入了CLOD场景-锁定初始化,将锚地初始化参数化为连续场(Sec.3.2.
在不同的密度上取样这个场会产生不同的锚数.
这使得场景的计数与参考视图计数脱钩,让我们的模型可以在不同的存储和渲染预算下运行.

blocks.en:
A compact scene representation should consolidate multi-view observations and allocate capacity where it is most useful.
To achieve this, we (1) use unified, scene-centric 3D anchors to consolidate redundant multi-view tokens, and (2) learn the spatial allocation of these anchors end-to-end.
Specifically, we use an end-to-end learned, geometry-grounded condenser that aggregates reference-view tokens into 3D anchors (Sec. 3.3 ).
The condenser predicts geometry for both views and anchors and uses their geometric relationships to guide cross-attention.
The resulting anchors have 3D positions, which further enable target-view frustum culling to reduce decoding cost (Sec. 3.4 ).
Both the geometry and scene-complexity-aware anchor allocation emerge from the NVS objective (Sec. 4.6 ).

为了实现这一目标,我们(1)使用统一,以场景为中心的3D锚地来整合冗余多景符号,(2)学习这些锚地的空间相接相接相接.
具体来说,我们使用一个端到端的有学问,几何定位的收缩器来将参考-视图符号聚合为3D锚(Sec.3.3.
收缩器预言了两种观点和锚地的几何特征,并利用其几何关系来指导交叉意向.
由此而来的主锚有3D位置,这进一步使靶景浮雕可以降低解码成本(Sec.3.4.).
几何学和场景-复杂-意识锚地分配均出自NVS目标(Sec 4.6.).

blocks.en:
We evaluate GLoD-LVSM across datasets, reference-view counts and scene-token budgets.
Quantitatively, GLoD-LVSM consistently achieves the best quality–token-count trade-off among the baselines.
Qualitatively, the learned anchors emerge near scene surfaces and allocate higher density to regions with richer texture, suggesting that NVS supervision and compression alone can induce a geometry- and complexity-aware efficient scene representation.
Beyond rendering, we further evaluate the learned representation on scene-semantic understanding, demonstrating its potential as a 3D scene representation for broader downstream tasks.
Our contributions are threefold: • Continuous-LoD scene representation. We introduce a scene-conditioned continuous query field that enables flexible scene anchor budgets independent of the reference-view count. • Geometry-grounded scene condensation. We learn scene-centric 3D anchors end-to-end, enabling efficient multi-view consolidation and scene-adaptive capacity allocation. • Efficient and generalizable scene anchors. GLoD-LVSM achieves the best quality–scene-token trade-off for rendering and supports scene semantic understanding.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Novel View Synthesis
blocks.zh: 2.1 小说视图合成

blocks.en:
Novel view synthesis (NVS) is a widely studied problem and can be broadly categorized into per-scene optimization methods and feed-forward generalizable methods.
NeRF ( Mildenhall et al., 2020 ) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) achieve photorealistic novel-view synthesis by optimizing a radiance field or a set of Gaussian primitives for each scene.
However, they typically require time-consuming per-scene optimization and dense image capture to achieve high rendering quality.
In contrast, generalizable NVS methods ( Sajjadi et al., 2022 ; Chen et al., 2024 ; Xu et al., 2025 ) , including recent Transformer-based approaches such as LVSMs ( Jin et al., 2025 ; Kim et al., 2026 ; Sun et al., 2026 ; Szymanowicz et al., 2026 ) , learn reconstruction priors from large datasets and can reconstruct unseen scenes from sparse input views in a single feed-forward pass, avoiding costly dense image capture and per-scene optimization.
Our work builds on Transformer-based generalizable NVS and focuses on learning a compact, geometry-grounded scene representation that reduces redundancy among scene tokens, thereby lowering storage and rendering costs.

小说取景合成(NVS)是一个被广泛研究的问题,可以被广泛归类为人均场景优化方法和饲料向上通俗的方法.
NERF(Mildenhall等,2020年)和3D高斯平板电脑(3DGS)(Kerbl等,2023年)通过优化风光场或为每个场景提供一套高斯平板电脑实现光现实主义小说-视觉合成.
然而,它们通常需要耗时的人均场景优化和密集的图像捕捉来达到高渲染质量.
与此相反,通用的NVS方法(Sajjadi等,2022;Chen等,2024;Xu等,2025),包括最近基于变形器的方法,如LVSMs(Jin等,2025;Kim等,2026;Sun等,2026;Szymanowicz等,2026),从大型数据集中学习重建的先兆,并可以在单一的向后传送的输入视图中从稀有的视角中再现出不见的场景,避免成本高昂的密集图像捕捉和场景优化.
我们的工作建立在以变形器为基础的可通用的NVS之上,并侧重于学习一种紧凑的几何定位的场景表现,减少场景符号之间的冗余,从而降低存储和渲染成本.

blocks.en: 2.2 Compact Scene Representation
blocks.zh: 2.2 契约场面代表

blocks.en:
Compact scene representations have been widely studied for efficient NVS.
For example, 3DGS methods prune or compress Gaussian primitives to reduce representation size while preserving visual quality ( Fan et al., 2024 ; Fang and Wang, 2024 ; Lin et al., 2025 ) .
Some methods further support multiple or continuous levels of detail (CLoD), allowing representation complexity to adapt to runtime rendering budgets ( Milef et al., 2025 ; Cheng et al., 2026 ) .
Compact scene-token representations have also been explored for LVSMs.
LVSM-ED ( Jin et al., 2025 ) uses a fixed latent bottleneck and cannot support flexible compression rates.
CLiFT ( Wang et al., 2025 ) uses K-means to select representative reference-view tokens, relying on handcrafted clustering that may be suboptimal.
Our work also targets compact scene representations for LVSMs. Unlike prior methods, we support CLoD and learn scene anchors end-to-end, enabling flexible compression with less handcrafted design.

CLIFT(Wang等,2025年)使用K-意指来选择具有代表性的参考-视图符号,依靠可能是次优的手工集群.

blocks.en: 3.2 Contextualized Continuous Field for Anchor Initialization
blocks.zh: 3.2 锁定初始化的背景化连续字段

blocks.en:
Given reference-view tokens 𝒁 {\bm{Z}} , our condenser compresses them into scene anchors.
The first challenge is anchor initialization.
Fixed learned vectors ( Jin et al., 2025 ) support only a predefined anchor count.
Clustering-based initialization ( Wang et al., 2025 ) supports variable counts, but relies on handcrafted clustering that may be suboptimal and remains image-centric rather than scene-centric.
We instead learn a scene-conditioned continuous initialization field end-to-end with minimal handcrafted design (Fig. 2 (a)).
Sampling the field at different densities yields different anchor budgets, enabling continuous levels of detail under varying storage and rendering constraints.

blocks.en: 3.3 Geometry-Grounded Bidirectional Condensation

blocks.en:
As illustrated in Fig. 2 (b), our condenser maps K K initialized anchors and N N reference-view tokens 𝒁 {\bm{Z}} to K K compact scene anchors.

blocks.en:
After geometry prediction, each condenser block first applies self-attention to the anchor stream, followed by bidirectional cross-attention between anchors and reference-view tokens and MLPs.
We inject the inferred geometry into this cross-attention using geometry-dependent RoPE.

Efficiency gains must be considered in the context of rendering quality.
Using LagerNVS-FT as the quality reference, we measure scene-token reduction under PSNR losses of X ∈ { 2 , 1 , 0.5 , 0 } X\in\{2,1,0.5,0\} dB.
Fig. 10 shows the results.
On 10-view RealEstate10K, GLoD-LVSM reduces the scene-token count by 85.5% at a 2 dB quality loss. Even with no quality loss (0 dB), it still reduces the token count by 33.4%, which we attribute to the more effective geometry-grounded representation. The corresponding rendering speedups are 3.00 × 3.00\times and 1.23 × 1.23\times over LagerNVS-FT , respectively. With culling, the estimated speedups further increase to 3.20 × 3.20\times and 1.55 × 1.55\times .

blocks.en: 4.5 Scaling Quality with Views and Beyond the Highway Token Count

blocks.en:
We now highlight two properties of GLoD-LVSM .
First, unlike highway designs whose scene tokens grow with reference-view count, GLoD-LVSM can exploit more views at a fixed scene-token budget .
Fig. 10 shows that, at a fixed token budget, GLoD-LVSM generally improves with more views.
For example, on RealEstate10K with a 2048-token budget, 10 views outperform 2 views by 2.8 dB.
In contrast, a 10-view highway model requires over 13K tokens.
At small capacity, such as 512 tokens, gains saturate/degrade beyond 6 views.

blocks.en:
To understand GLoD-LVSM , we visualize its representation using four reference views with 2048 scene anchors (Fig. 1 ).
Without explicit geometry supervision, consistent scene depth emerges across reference views, while the learned anchors concentrate near scene surfaces.
Projecting the anchors back onto the reference images further reveals scene-adaptive allocation: anchors are denser in texture-rich regions and sparser in textureless regions.
These results show that the NVS loss can induce an efficient geometry- and texture-aware scene representation.
More visualizations are in Supplementary Figs. S26 – S31 .

blocks.en: 4.8 GLoD-LVSM Supports Scene Semantic Understanding
blocks.zh: 4.8 GLOD-LVSM 支持场景语义理解

blocks.en:
We further examine whether the learned anchors capture scene semantics beyond rendering.
We use VLM-generated annotations for RealEstate10K ( He et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2023 ) to categorize scenes into eight semantic classes.
For each scene, GLoD-LVSM compresses 10 reference views into 1,024 anchors, which are mean-pooled into a single 768-dimensional scene vector .
We train only a linear probe on this vector for scene classification and achieve 80.40%/91.73% top-1/top-2 accuracy.
This result shows that learned anchors already contain scene semantics.
See Supplementary A.6 for evaluation protocol and
Supplementary Fig. S2 for the confusion matrix.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We propose GLoD-LVSM , a compact, geometry-grounded LVSM representation with continuous levels of detail. GLoD-LVSM achieves a strong quality–token trade-off through two key designs: (1) an end-to-end learned continuous field with minimal handcrafted design, and (2) a condenser that consolidates multi-view observations into scene-centric, geometry-grounded anchors.
Trained with the NVS objective, GLoD-LVSM learns geometry- and texture-aware anchor allocation.
We further show its utility on scene semantic understanding, highlighting the potential beyond rendering.
blocks.zh:
我们提出GLOD-LVSM, 一种紧凑的,几何定位的LVSM代表, 持续的详细程度。 GLOD-LVSM通过两个关键设计实现强烈的质量-托克取舍:(1)一个端到端所学的连续场,手动设计最少;(2)一个将多视图观测整合成以场景为中心,几何定位的锚地的收缩器.
GLOD-LVSM通过NVS目标培训,学习几何和纹理意识锚地分配.
我们进一步展示了它在现场语义理解上的效用,突出了渲染之外的潜力.

blocks.en: A.4 Depth Denoising for Point-Cloud Visualization

blocks.en:
To visualize the noisy predicted reference-view depth as a point cloud, we apply a 3 × 3 3\times 3 median filter to the patch-level depth and upsample it to image resolution using joint bilateral upsampling ( Kopf et al., 2007 ) guided by the corresponding RGB image.
We then back-project the filtered depth using the camera intrinsics, transform the points into a shared scene coordinate system using the camera poses, and color them with RGB values.
This post-processing is used only for point-cloud visualization; the displayed depth maps are raw predictions, and the model geometry, anchors, and rendering remain unchanged.

然后我们用相机内在的来回投影滤波深度, 利用相机的姿势把点变成共享的场景坐标系统, 用RGB值来涂色。
此后处理仅用于点-相克可视化;所显示的深度图为原始预测,模型几何,锚地,渲染不变.

blocks.en: A.5 Rendering-Speed Evaluation
blocks.zh: A.5 评价

blocks.en:
We report results for GLoD-LVSM both with and without culling in Fig. S1 .
We evaluate rendering speed on an NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU using BF16 with a batch size of 1 and 1 target view.
For the baseline and our no-culling model, we directly benchmark rendering latency at fixed scene-token counts.
For the culling-enabled model, the effective decoder-token count varies across scenes and target poses.
We therefore estimate its speed by measuring rendering speed at the average post-culling decoder-token count over the test set.
The estimated rendering latency includes the measured culling overhead.

我们报告GLOD-LVSM的结果,
我们利用批量大小为1和1目标视图的BF16,在一款NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU上评价渲染速度.
对于基线和我们的无堆积模型, 我们直接基准 使延迟在固定的现场计数。
对于Culling-uplied的模型,有效的解码器-托克计数因场景和靶姿而异.
因此,我们估计其速度,方法是在测试组上测量平均的燃烧后解码器-托肯计数的渲染速度。
